closingKeywordWhy: This PR is a slice of #1138: only the four review suggestions deferred from the MVP PR. The intake adapters (harness incident-response records, SARIF, pasted pen-test findings) and the Java/Go/Ruby/.NET trace formats stay open in #1138.
assumptions: Brainstorming sign-off was taken autonomously (fleet lane default): decisions C1-C8 in the spec took the recommended option. No fork was parked.

C1/C2: in a chained exception the signature and the suspect stay on the reported (outermost) error, which is what the runner prints and verify anchors on. The chain is added information: a list with the root cause marked, boundary lines in the frame list, and one requirement sentence naming the root cause and where it was raised.

C3: the chain is an optional side list (ParsedTrace.chain / RegressionBrief.chain) whose `start` indexes into the existing flat frames list. An unchained trace's brief is unchanged (no `chain` key); the schema stays canary-judomaster-brief/1 because the field is additive. If any CPython block has frames but no error line, the chain is dropped and the trace parses exactly as before.

C4 (recommended default from the lane brief): verify does NOT auto-fetch a runner. It runs `npx --no` in place of `npx --yes` / `-y`, and npx's 'canceled due to missing packages' refusal is `unverified — could not reproduce` (exit 3) with the runner named. Nothing in the MVP depends on fetching. The rewrite is an opt-in executor option (`fetch: false`) set only by verify; `canary run` and MCP `run_tests` keep the registry command as is.
C5: the runner is spawned with cwd = realpath of --root (default still the process cwd).

C6/C7: mocking the suspect module is a WARNING only; the verdict and exit code are unchanged. It needs the brief's suspect, so without --brief no check runs. It reads the test file's own source, not siblings. It assumes brief and verify use the same --root (the suspect path is root-relative); the guide says so.
C8: one isWithin() helper built on path.relative() replaces both string-prefix containment checks (frame resolution and tests/generated).
mockedSuspectWarnings lives in resolve.ts rather than a new module (entropy ratchet: no new source files) and to keep verify.ts under the 300-line perf threshold.

Ratchets measured locally with harness CLI 12.10.1 against a detached worktree of the merge base 37918569: entropy 141 vs 141 (delta OK), perf 216 vs 216 (0 new findings), check-arch newViolations [] on both trees. After the review fixes module-size measured 50179 against 49675 (+504, the only regression), so an allowance was added (.harness/arch/allowances/feat-1138-judomaster-review-followups.json) and the floor refreshed with scripts/refresh-arch-baseline.mjs (violationIds untouched), as #614 did. No entryPoints added; maxFindings untouched.

Autopilot ran at fast rigor (single phase, 10 tasks, plan auto-approved): planning via harness-planner, tasks 1-9 via harness-task-executor, ratchets (task 10) by the lane, final review via harness-code-reviewer.

Review amendments (harness-code-reviewer: 0 critical, 1 important, 7 suggestions): the mock warning is strong only for a whole-module mock or a patch of the suspect function, and soft ('check it is a dependency') for a JS partial mock (importOriginal/requireActual/spy: true) or a Python patch of another name inside the module; bare JS specifiers need a '/' or an @/ ~/ alias; commented-out mocks are ignored; the npx refusal is read only from npm's own stderr line on a non-zero exit; a frameless CPython cause block takes its last error line; a frameless trailing cause gets a boundary marker and an empty message renders without a colon. Not taken (left as suggestions): a link for a [cause]: header that is not an error line (e.g. DOMException [AbortError]) - such causes merge into the outer error as before; directory-index suspects, vi.mock(import(...)), jest.unstable_mockModule and src-layout top-level Python modules are not detected.

Behaviour change noted in the CHANGELOG: the V8 frame regex now accepts a trailing ' {', so a Node error with own properties (e.g. a system error's code) keeps its outermost frame instead of dropping it, even when unchained.
